newsitem.title: USA: Sun still rises on Hemingway look-alike contest.
newsitem.headline: Sun still rises on Hemingway look-alike contest.

text.p: Sloppy Joe's bar defiantly said on Thursday it would stage its annual Ernest Hemingway look-alike contest despite cancellation of Key West's Hemingway festival because of a dispute with the late author's family.

"It's going to go on. We at the bar are going to run it. There was a lot of disappointment that it was cancelled so now we're trying to get the word out," Sloppy Joe's promotions manager Ray Larsen told Reuters on Thursday.
The look-alike contest was the highlight of the festival, drawing dozens of portly, white-bearded Papa 'wanna-bes' to the bar on Key West's Duvall Street where Hemingway often drank.

Organisers of the fiesta, which also included an arm-wrestling contest and writing competitons, cancelled it this month after Hemingway's son Patrick said certain activities were not a fitting tribute to the Nobel laureate and demanded a share of the profits.
"This has nothing to do with festival," Larsen said.
The competition will be from July 24-26.
Hemingway lived in Key West from 1929 to 1940, penning such works as "Death in the Afternoon" and "The Snows of Kilimanjaro."
